itineraries.title: First Friday, On Foot — Downtown Raleigh
itineraries.theme: One free, self-guided art walk that turns the whole downtown grid into a gallery, then a movie on Moore Square and a late DJ set
itineraries.drive_time: Park once and walk. Everything here sits inside a 12-block square between Glenwood Ave and Blount St; the longest hop (Gallery C on N Blount to Moore Square) is about 15 minutes on foot or 5 by car.

weather.summary: Mostly Sunny then Slight Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $0–$40 (the art walk, Artspace, Gallery C, the Pope House social, the Moore Square movie and Curate's market are all free; you only spend on food, drinks and parking)
itineraries.overview: August 7 is First Friday, when Downtown Raleigh's galleries, studios and museums stay open late for free. It hits 91°F, so this route front-loads the air-conditioned stops and saves the outdoor legs for after 7 PM once the sun is off the buildings. Storms are possible late afternoon — every leg here has an indoor twin within two blocks.

afternoon.title: Artist/Curatorial Discussion with Sam van Strien
afternoon.notes: Start here — it's the one timed talk of the evening. The artist walks the show and its engagement with the Tennessee Valley Authority's legacy.

afternoon.title: First Friday at Slim's Downtown
afternoon.location: Slim's Downtown, 227 S Wilmington St, Raleigh
afternoon.notes: Opens earliest of the bar stops. Malort tasting, live jazz and art on the walls; the patio is the late-night option if you circle back.

afternoon.title: Artspace First Friday
afternoon.notes: Three floors of working studios open until 10 PM. The 4–6 PM window is the sensory-friendly one — smaller crowds, no amplified music.

evening.title: Ice Cream Social at Pope House Museum
evening.location: Dr. M.T. Pope House Museum, 511 S Wilmington St, Raleigh
evening.notes: The preserved home of Dr. Manassa Thomas Pope, the only Black man to run for mayor of a Southern capital during Jim Crow. Small house, short visit, real history — and ice cream.

evening.title: First Friday Raleigh Gallery Walk
evening.notes: The umbrella event, 6–9 PM. No ticket, no route — just walk. Pick up the Gallery C and Carter Building stops below as you go.

evening.title: Gallery C: Marsha Burns Silver Gelatin Photography
evening.location: Gallery C, 540 N Blount St, Raleigh
evening.notes: The northernmost stop and the quietest. Worth the walk up Blount if you want to actually look at work rather than move through a crowd.

evening.title: Curate Raleigh Handmade Market
evening.location: Curate Raleigh, 15 W Hargett St, Raleigh
evening.notes: Forty-plus local makers plus a coffee popup. Indoors and air-conditioned — a good reset between gallery stops.

evening.title: First Friday Market and Movie at Moore Square
evening.location: Moore Square, 200 S Blount St, Raleigh
evening.notes: Free outdoor movie with a vendor market, food trucks and live music, 5–9 PM. Bring a blanket. This is the leg that storms would cancel — check the sky before you commit.

evening.title: First Friday Live Music and Vendor Market at The Raleigh Times
evening.location: The Raleigh Times Bar, 14 E Hargett St, Raleigh
evening.notes: Live music and a market in the old newspaper building. The indoor answer if Moore Square gets rained out — it's a three-minute walk.

evening.title: Late Night DJ Dance Party at Neptunes Parlour
evening.location: Neptunes Parlour, 14 W Martin St, Raleigh
evening.notes: The basement under Kings, running to 2 AM. 21+. Skip if you want an early night — everything above wraps by 10.

food.vegan_dish: Build a plate across stalls — the falafel and hummus counters plate vegan without substitutions; ask each stall directly, as the vendor lineup rotates
food.vegetarian_dish: Wood-fired margherita or a cheese-and-veg sandwich from the deli counter
food.notes: Ten minutes east of the gallery district at 500 E Davie St. Multiple kitchens under one roof, which is the easy answer when the group can't agree. Confirm today's stalls at the door.

food.vegan_dish: Ask the kitchen which of the bar sides are made without butter — the fries and the pickled vegetables usually are
food.vegetarian_dish: Pimento cheese and a beer, in the room where the newspaper used to set type
food.notes: Alternative if you want to stay on Hargett Street for the vendor market. Gets loud and full after 8 on a First Friday.

alternatives.leg: Moore Square outdoor movie and market (7 PM)
alternatives.good_weather: Blanket on the lawn at Moore Square for the free film, market and food trucks.
alternatives.rain: Walk three minutes to The Raleigh Times for indoor live music and the vendor market, or duck into Artspace, which stays open to 10 PM.

alternatives.good_weather: Do the full Blount-to-Glenwood loop on foot; it's about 25 minutes end to end.
alternatives.rain: Cluster tightly: Artspace, Curate and The Raleigh Times sit within three blocks of each other and are all indoors.

practical_notes: First Friday is free and unticketed — there is nothing to book. Just show up.
City decks on Wilmington and Blount are free after 5 PM on Fridays; street parking downtown is also free after 5.
91°F and humid at 4 PM, easing after sunset. Carry water — most galleries have none.
Neptunes is 21+; everything else on this route is all-ages.
Slim's, Le Dive and Neptunes are within one block of each other on Martin and Wilmington if you want to extend the night.

itineraries.title: Stars and Giant Puppets — Chapel Hill & Carrboro
itineraries.theme: A morning at the oldest producer-only market in the state, an afternoon hiding from 91°F under a planetarium dome, and Paperhand's giant puppets in an outdoor stone amphitheatre at dusk
itineraries.drive_time: ~35 min from downtown Raleigh to Carrboro. Once there everything is close: Carrboro Town Commons to Morehead Planetarium is 8 min, Morehead to the Forest Theatre is 5 min or a 12-minute walk.

weather.summary: Mostly Sunny then Slight Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $25–$70 per person (markets free; planetarium shows ticketed; Paperhand is pay-what-you-can at the gate with a suggested range)
itineraries.overview: Saturday tops out near 91°F, so this day is built around the shade: an early market before the heat lands, a planetarium dome through the worst of the afternoon, then Paperhand Puppet Intervention's 26th annual summer show in the Forest Theatre once the sun drops behind the trees. The market opens at 7 AM — going early is the whole trick.

morning.title: Carrboro Farmers' Market
morning.location: Carrboro Town Commons, 301 W Main St, Carrboro
morning.notes: Opens at 7 and runs to noon. One of the oldest producer-only markets in North Carolina — everything sold here is grown or made by the person selling it. Go before 9 while it's under 80°F.

morning.title: Magic Tree House Space Mission
morning.location: Morehead Planetarium and Science Center, 250 E Franklin St, Chapel Hill
morning.notes: The youngest-skewing show of the day. Skip it if your group is all adults and start at the noon slot instead.

afternoon.title: Star Families
afternoon.location: Morehead Planetarium and Science Center, Chapel Hill
afternoon.notes: Fulldome show on how stars are born and die. Buy planetarium tickets online — individual showtimes sell out on hot Saturdays for exactly this reason.

afternoon.title: Phantom of the Universe
afternoon.location: Morehead Planetarium and Science Center, Chapel Hill
afternoon.notes: The dark-matter documentary. Pick one or two shows, not all four — the dome is comfortable but four hours in a reclined seat is a lot.

afternoon.title: Carolina Skies
afternoon.location: Morehead Planetarium and Science Center, Chapel Hill
afternoon.notes: Live presenter, not a recording — they walk the actual sky you'll see over Chapel Hill tonight. The best primer before an outdoor evening.

evening.title: Paperhand Puppet Intervention: The Wild Wisdom of the World
evening.location: Forest Theatre, 123 South Boundary St, Chapel Hill
evening.notes: Openers at 6:20, Paperhand at 7. Their 26th annual summer show — giant puppets, masks, stilts, shadow work and a live band in a 1940s stone amphitheatre. Bring a blanket or a low chair and arrive early for a decent spot.

food.vegan_dish: Hot bar and salad bar are labelled by diet — the tofu scramble and the roasted-vegetable sides are the reliable vegan picks
food.vegetarian_dish: Pastry and coffee on the lawn, which is the actual Carrboro Saturday ritual
food.notes: Directly beside the Town Commons, so it's the same stop as the market. Sit on the lawn; the whole town does.

food.vegan_dish: Chana masala or the daily vegan curry — the kitchen cooks a large part of the menu vegan by default and marks it on the board
food.vegetarian_dish: Saag paneer with rice and naan
food.notes: In Courtyard off Franklin Street, a five-minute walk from Morehead. Confirm the day's vegan curry at the counter — it rotates.

food.place: Al's Burger Shack or a picnic at the Forest Theatre
food.vegan_dish: Pack it in — the Forest Theatre allows outside food, and Weaver Street's hot bar travels well
food.vegetarian_dish: Veggie burger on Franklin Street before you walk over
food.notes: Eating at the amphitheatre before the show is the local move. There is no concession stand worth planning around.

alternatives.leg: Paperhand at the Forest Theatre (6:20 PM)
alternatives.good_weather: Outdoor stone amphitheatre under the trees — arrive by 6 for a seat near the front.
alternatives.rain: Paperhand performs rain or shine unless there's lightning; bring a poncho rather than an umbrella (it blocks the view behind you). If it's called off, Cat's Cradle Back Room in Carrboro has Jack The Songman the night before and Local 506 has Money Shot with Tiger Knives at 8 PM the same night.

alternatives.good_weather: Full outdoor market on the Town Commons.
alternatives.rain: The market runs in light rain under the shed roofs; Weaver Street next door is fully indoors.

practical_notes: Buy Morehead planetarium tickets online before you leave — showtimes are individually ticketed and the hot-Saturday slots go.
Forest Theatre parking is limited and street parking around South Boundary fills by 6. Park on campus and walk if you're arriving late.
91°F with afternoon storm chances: the 12–5 block is deliberately indoors.
The Forest Theatre is stone-terraced and uneven — a low chair beats a blanket if anyone in the group has knees to protect.
Carrboro market takes cards at most stalls but a few growers are cash-only.

itineraries.title: Farm Stand to Jerk Festival — Durham
itineraries.theme: Saturday morning at the Central Park pavilion, two of the most serious historic sites in the state at midday, and a Caribbean food festival back where you started
itineraries.drive_time: ~30 min from downtown Raleigh to Durham Central Park. Bennett Place is 10 min west of downtown Durham; Stagville is 20 min north. Budget the drive time — the two historic sites are on opposite sides of the city.

weather.summary: Mostly Sunny then Slight Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $5–$45 per person (market free, Bennett Place $1–$4, Stagville $2, Jerk Festival admission unconfirmed — bring cash for food)
itineraries.overview: A Durham Saturday that starts under the Central Park pavilion at 8 AM and ends at the NC Jerk Festival on the same lawn six hours later. In between, two historic sites that tell the hardest and most important parts of the region's history — and both cost less than a coffee. It's 91°F: the historic sites are partly outdoors, and Bennett Place warns tours can be shortened in extreme heat.

morning.title: Durham Farmers' Market
morning.location: Durham Central Park Pavilion, 501 Foster St, Durham
morning.notes: 8 AM to noon under the pavilion. Producer-only. This is the same lawn the Jerk Festival takes over at 3, so you can scout parking now.

morning.title: Bennett Place Guided Tour
morning.location: Bennett Place State Historic Site, 4409 Bennett Memorial Rd, Durham
morning.notes: The farmhouse where Johnston surrendered to Sherman in April 1865 — the largest surrender of the Civil War, larger than Appomattox. First tour of the day and the coolest slot.

morning.title: Historic Stagville Guided Tour
morning.location: Historic Stagville State Historic Site, 5828 Old Oxford Hwy, Durham
morning.notes: Alternative to Bennett Place rather than an addition — they're 30 minutes apart. Stagville was one of the largest plantations in the antebellum South, and the tour centres the lives of the people enslaved there. Saturday tours at 11, 1 and 3.

afternoon.title: NC Jerk Festival
afternoon.location: Durham Central Park, 501 Foster St, Durham
afternoon.notes: 3–9 PM. Caribbean food, music and dancing on the Central Park lawn. This is the anchor — everything else is optional around it.

afternoon.title: Taste Carolina Durham Food Tour
afternoon.notes: Conflicts with the Jerk Festival — pick one. The walking tour is the better choice if the forecast turns and you'd rather be moving between indoor restaurants than standing on a lawn.

evening.title: Beer Garden Concert Series with Heavy Weather
evening.location: The Glass Jug Beer Lab (RTP), 5410 NC-55, Durham
evening.notes: If you skipped the Jerk Festival or want a quieter finish: 20 minutes south in RTP, outdoor beer garden, live band 6–9.

food.vegan_dish: Several bakers keep a vegan pastry case; the produce stalls make the best breakfast anyway — peaches and tomatoes are at peak in early August
food.vegetarian_dish: Breakfast biscuit from one of the market vendors
food.notes: Eat at the market. Ask each stall directly — vendors rotate week to week and labelling is inconsistent.

food.vegan_dish: Any wood-fired pizza built on the vegan cheese, plus the antipasti and salads, which are largely vegan as served
food.vegetarian_dish: Margherita from the wood oven
food.notes: 105 E Chapel Hill St, five minutes from Central Park. Confirm the vegan cheese is on hand — it's a standing option but not always stocked.

food.vegan_dish: Ital plates — the Rastafarian vegan tradition is a genuine part of Caribbean cooking, so ask vendors for ital; several usually serve it alongside the jerk
food.vegetarian_dish: Rice and peas, festival dumplings, plantains and callaloo from the vendor stalls
food.notes: Bring cash. Vendor lineups at one-day festivals aren't published in advance, so treat specific dishes as likely rather than guaranteed.

alternatives.leg: NC Jerk Festival (3–9 PM, outdoor lawn)
alternatives.good_weather: Full afternoon and evening on the Central Park lawn.
alternatives.rain: Swap to the Taste Carolina Durham food tour at 3 PM, which moves between indoor restaurants, or head to the Carolina Theatre — The Wallflowers play Fletcher Hall the following night.

alternatives.good_weather: Do the full Stagville tour including the Horton Grove quarters, which is a walk across open ground.
alternatives.rain: Bennett Place has more indoor interpretation and a visitor centre; it's the better wet-weather pick of the two.

practical_notes: Bennett Place explicitly warns that summer tours are sometimes shortened or cancelled in extreme heat — call 984-250-1322 the morning of if it's already 90°F by 10 AM.
Bennett Place and Stagville are 30 minutes apart on opposite sides of Durham. Pick one unless you're happy driving.
Both historic sites are closed Sunday and Monday; Saturday is the day with the fullest tour schedule.
Durham Central Park has free street parking in the surrounding blocks on weekends, but it fills fast once the festival starts at 3.
The market ends at noon sharp — vendors sell out of the good tomatoes well before that.

itineraries.title: Free Museums to Amphitheater — Raleigh
itineraries.theme: A 75-acre farmers market at dawn, two free state museums through the heat of the day, and an outdoor amphitheatre show downtown
itineraries.drive_time: All inside Raleigh. State Farmers Market to the NCMA is 12 min; NCMA to the State Capitol is 15 min; Capitol to Red Hat Amphitheater is a 10-minute walk.

weather.summary: Mostly Sunny then Slight Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $0–$95 (market, NCMA, birding and the Capitol program are free; the Untold tour is $25 and the amphitheatre show is ticketed)
itineraries.overview: Raleigh's free institutions do a lot of work on a 91°F Saturday. Start with birding in the NCMA Museum Park at 8 AM before it's hot, spend the middle of the day inside two free state museums, and finish outdoors at Red Hat Amphitheater once the sun is behind the buildings. Slight storm chance late afternoon — the museum legs are the hedge.

morning.title: State Farmers Market
morning.location: State Farmers Market, 1201 Agriculture St, Raleigh
morning.notes: Open seven days, from 5 AM. Seventy-five acres of growers' sheds, a garden centre and a restaurant. Early August is peak tomato and peach season here.

morning.title: Birding with Wake Audubon Society
morning.location: NCMA Museum Park, 2110 Blue Ridge Rd, Raleigh
morning.notes: Two hours in the Museum Park with Wake Audubon volunteers. The only comfortable outdoor window of the day — it's under 80°F until about 10.

afternoon.title: Ancient Inspirations
afternoon.location: North Carolina State Capitol, 1 E Edenton St, Raleigh
afternoon.notes: An hour on the classical sources behind the 1840 Capitol's architecture. The building itself is the exhibit, and it's free to walk.

afternoon.title: Public Tour
afternoon.location: North Carolina Museum of Art, Raleigh
afternoon.notes: Alternative to the Capitol program at the same hour — a free docent walk through the NCMA collection if you'd rather stay on Blue Ridge Road.

afternoon.title: Museum Untold Tour
afternoon.location: NC Museum of Natural Sciences, 11 W Jones St, Raleigh
afternoon.notes: The one paid stop, and the most interesting: a guided tour of the stories the museum's main exhibits leave out. Book ahead — it runs only on select Saturdays.

afternoon.title: Art on the Dot
afternoon.location: North Carolina Museum of Art, Raleigh
afternoon.notes: Drop-in art-making, 2:30–4:30, fully air-conditioned. The natural place to be when the afternoon peaks — and the family-friendly branch of this day.

evening.title: Stephen Wilson Jr. — Gary the Torch Tour with The Lone Bellow
evening.location: Red Hat Amphitheater, 500 S McDowell St, Raleigh
evening.notes: Outdoor amphitheatre in the middle of downtown. Doors are before 7; the walk from the Capitol is 10 minutes if you've been downtown all afternoon.

evening.title: Dom Flemons Presents the Bronze Buckaroo Film and Songster Show
evening.location: North Carolina Museum of Art, Raleigh
evening.notes: Indoor alternative and arguably the better show: the Grammy-winning songster pairs Black-cowboy cinema with live roots music. Start time is listed only as evening — confirm on the NCMA page.

food.vegan_dish: Grits and fruit from the market sheds is the honest vegan answer here — this is a traditional Southern breakfast counter
food.vegetarian_dish: Eggs, grits and biscuits
food.notes: On the market grounds. Opens early and fills with growers before it fills with shoppers. Not a vegan-forward kitchen — plan around the produce stalls if that matters.

food.vegan_dish: Ask which of the day's vegetable sides are cooked without pork — several usually are, and they'll tell you straight
food.vegetarian_dish: A plate of vegetable sides — collards, mac, candied yams
food.notes: Downtown on the way between the Capitol and the Natural Sciences museum. Meat-and-three format, so the vegetable plate is a real menu item, not a compromise.

food.vegan_dish: Multiple stalls plate vegan — the poke and the Mediterranean counters are the usual bets; ask at each
food.vegetarian_dish: Pizza, arepas or noodles depending on the stall lineup
food.notes: Five minutes' walk from Red Hat Amphitheater, which makes it the obvious pre-show stop. Arrive before 6 on a show night.

alternatives.leg: Red Hat Amphitheater show (7 PM, outdoor)
alternatives.good_weather: Open-air amphitheatre with the downtown skyline behind the stage.
alternatives.rain: Switch to the Dom Flemons show indoors at the NCMA, or Cosmic Charlie at Lincoln Theatre at 8:30 PM — both indoors and both a few minutes away.

alternatives.leg: Morning birding in the Museum Park (8 AM, outdoor)
alternatives.good_weather: Two hours walking the park loop with Wake Audubon.
alternatives.rain: Go straight to the NCMA galleries, which open before the tour slots and are free.

practical_notes: The NCMA, the State Capitol and the NC Museum of Natural Sciences are all free — this day can cost nothing but parking and food.
Book the Museum Untold Tour ahead; it's capacity-limited and only runs select Saturdays.
NCMA parking is free. Downtown decks are free on Saturdays; the Red Hat lots are not on show nights.
91°F with a slight storm chance after 3 PM. The 1–4:30 block is deliberately indoors.
If you're doing both the Capitol program and the Untold Tour, they're a 10-minute walk apart on the same downtown block — no need to move the car.

itineraries.title: Free Museum Day — Durham with Kids
itineraries.theme: 84 acres of science museum free for Durham residents, a Black farmers market, and a treasure hunt that turns downtown into a game board
itineraries.drive_time: ~30 min from downtown Raleigh. Museum of Life and Science to Durham Central Park is 8 min; Central Park to Durham Tech is 10 min.

weather.summary: Mostly Sunny then Slight Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $0 for Durham County residents with ID; otherwise $23 adult / $18 child for the museum, everything else free
itineraries.overview: August 9 is a Durham Community Day at the Museum of Life and Science — Durham County residents get in free with proof of residency, and each adult can bring up to five children. At 93°F this is the hottest day of the week, so the plan is: outdoor museum exhibits early, indoor exhibits at midday, and a downtown treasure hunt in the late afternoon when the shade returns.

morning.title: Museum of Life and Science: Durham Community Day
morning.location: Museum of Life and Science, 433 W Murray Ave, Durham
morning.price: Free for Durham County residents with proof of residence; otherwise $23 adult / $18 child
morning.notes: Open 10–5. Arrive at opening and do the outdoor half first — Dinosaur Trail, the farmyard and the train are miserable after noon in this heat. The Butterfly House is indoors and humid but shaded.

afternoon.title: Black Farmers Market (Durham)
afternoon.location: Durham Technical Community College, 1637 E Lawson St, Durham
afternoon.notes: First and third Sundays, 1–4 PM. Black growers, makers and food vendors from across the Triangle. A short, worthwhile stop between the museum and downtown.

afternoon.title: Second Sundays: Open Studio
afternoon.location: Nasher Museum of Art at Duke University, 2001 Campus Dr, Durham
afternoon.notes: Free drop-in art studio, materials provided, 1–3 PM. Fully air-conditioned — the best indoor alternative if the museum wore everyone out.

afternoon.title: Bull City Treasure Hunt
afternoon.location: Durham Central Park, 501 Foster St, Durham
afternoon.notes: Runs 1–7 PM, so a 3 PM start still leaves four hours. Clues route through downtown Durham on foot — start late and you'll be walking in shade.

evening.title: Ice cream and the walk back
evening.notes: No ticketed evening event on this route by design — 93°F with kids is a full day. The Wallflowers play the Carolina Theatre at 8 PM if you have a sitter.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan doughnuts are a standing part of the case — ask which flavours are vegan that morning, as they rotate daily
food.vegetarian_dish: Egg-and-cheese biscuit or a cake doughnut
food.notes: 1002 9th St, on the way to the museum. The line moves; go before 9 on a Sunday.

food.place: Museum of Life and Science cafe or a packed cooler
food.vegan_dish: Pack it — museum cafes are not where you want to solve this, and the museum has shaded picnic areas
food.vegetarian_dish: Cafe sandwiches and snacks on site
food.notes: The museum allows outside food and has picnic tables. With five kids per adult permitted on Community Day, packing is the sane choice.

food.vegan_dish: Most rice and noodle bowls come with a choice of protein — order the tofu version
food.vegetarian_dish: Tofu bibimbap or a vegetable bowl
food.notes: Downtown, near where the treasure hunt ends. Confirm the sauce base with the kitchen if you're strictly vegan.

alternatives.leg: Museum of Life and Science outdoor exhibits (Dinosaur Trail, farmyard, train)
alternatives.good_weather: Do them first thing, 10 AM to noon, before the heat lands.
alternatives.rain: The indoor galleries and the Butterfly House cover the whole afternoon on their own; the museum is genuinely half indoors.

alternatives.leg: Bull City Treasure Hunt (outdoor, on foot)
alternatives.good_weather: Start at 3 PM and take the full downtown route.
alternatives.rain: Swap to Second Sundays: Open Studio at the Nasher, 1–3 PM, indoors and free.

practical_notes: Durham Community Day admission is free only with current proof of Durham County residency — bring a driver's licence or a utility bill. Guests without proof pay full price at check-in.
Each adult may bring up to five children free. All adults in the party need Durham residency.
93°F is the week's high. Museum staff recommend arriving early; the parking lot fills on Community Days.
The Nasher and the Museum of Life and Science are 10 minutes apart, so the indoor fallback is easy to reach mid-day.
The Black Farmers Market runs only 1–4 PM and only on first and third Sundays — it won't wait for you.

itineraries.title: Tomato Sunday — Pittsboro & Chatham County
itineraries.theme: A free tomato festival with a pie competition at the edge of the metro, bookended by an NCMA gallery talk on the way out and back
itineraries.drive_time: ~45 min from downtown Raleigh to Pittsboro, mostly on US-64. The Plant is 3 min south of the Pittsboro circle. This is the longest drive of the week's itineraries but still a comfortable same-day trip.

weather.summary: Mostly Sunny then Slight Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $0–$35 (the festival is free; you spend on food, drink and whatever you carry home from the craft market)
itineraries.overview: The Chatham Tomato Festival runs noon to 6 PM at The Plant, an old industrial site south of Pittsboro that now houses a brewery, a cidery and a cluster of small food businesses. Free entry, a tomato pie competition judged at 2 PM, heirloom-variety talks, garden tours and live music from Colby Jack & The High Lifes. It's 93°F and largely outdoors, so this one is genuinely a shade-and-water day.

morning.title: Notes on View: Eduardo de Rosamaria
morning.location: North Carolina Museum of Art, 2110 Blue Ridge Rd, Raleigh
morning.notes: A short in-gallery talk on a single work before you head west. The NCMA sits on the Raleigh side of the US-64 run, so it's genuinely on the way — leave by 11:45.

afternoon.title: Chatham Tomato Festival
afternoon.notes: Opening bell at noon, pie winner announced at 2 PM. Heirloom talks, garden tours, a craft market and live music through the afternoon. Free entry; food and drink are pay-as-you-go.

evening.title: Summer Concert Series
evening.location: Fred Fletcher Park, 820 Clay St, Raleigh
evening.notes: Free Raleigh Parks concert back in town if you leave Pittsboro by 5. Bring a blanket or a low chair.

evening.title: Jason Adamo Presents North Carolina Songwriters in the Round
evening.location: Lincoln Theatre, 126 E Cabarrus St, Raleigh
evening.notes: Indoor, ticketed alternative: eight North Carolina songwriters trading songs. Doors 5 PM, show 6 — a tight turnaround from Pittsboro, so buy ahead.

food.vegan_dish: Oat-milk latte with a granola bowl — ask which pastries are made without dairy that morning
food.vegetarian_dish: Egg-and-cheese biscuit
food.notes: Off Wade Ave near the NCMA, so it lines up with the 11 AM gallery talk. Menus rotate; confirm the plant-based option at the counter.

food.vegan_dish: A tomato festival in August is about as vegan-friendly as a food event gets — heirloom tomato plates, and Chatham County's growers cook produce-forward by default
food.vegetarian_dish: Tomato pie, which is the entire point of the day
food.notes: Eat at the festival. Vendor lineups for one-day events aren't published in advance, so treat specific dishes as likely rather than confirmed.

food.place: The Plant on-site brewery and cidery
food.vegan_dish: Cider and beer are the draw; food comes from the festival vendors rather than a fixed kitchen
food.vegetarian_dish: Whatever's left from the festival stalls, eaten in the shade
food.notes: Stay put rather than driving back hungry, or leave by 5 and eat in Raleigh before the Fletcher Park concert.

alternatives.good_weather: Full afternoon at The Plant — garden tours, the pie judging at 2, music into the evening.
alternatives.rain: The Plant has indoor taproom space at the brewery and cidery on site, so a passing storm doesn't end the day. If it's washed out entirely, the NCMA's Art on the Dot runs 2:30–4:30 indoors back in Raleigh.

alternatives.leg: Evening concert at Fred Fletcher Park (outdoor)
alternatives.good_weather: Free outdoor concert on the lawn.
alternatives.rain: Lincoln Theatre's NC Songwriters in the Round at 6 PM, indoors and ticketed.

practical_notes: The festival is free but parking at The Plant is limited — arrive near the noon opening or be ready to walk in from Lorax Lane.
93°F and mostly outdoors: this is the day to bring more water than you think you need.
Pie competition entry is free if you want to compete rather than just eat; judging is at 2 PM.
Chatham Mills Farmers Market runs Saturdays, not Sundays — don't plan on combining the two.
US-64 west from Raleigh is the fast route; allow extra time coming back if you're chasing a 6 PM show.

itineraries.title: Ballpark Thursday — Durham
itineraries.theme: Native-plant garden walk, a brewery anniversary that's actually a piece of state beer history, and Triple-A baseball under the lights
itineraries.drive_time: ~30 min from downtown Raleigh. Duke Gardens to Fullsteam is 8 min; Fullsteam to the Durham Bulls Athletic Park is a 10-minute walk or 3-minute drive.
itineraries.cost_range: $15–$50 per person (garden walk $10, ballpark tickets vary, beer extra)
itineraries.overview: A Thursday built around the Bulls' home series against the Memphis Redbirds. Start with a guided walk through Duke Gardens' native-plant collection in the late morning, spend the early evening at Fullsteam for the 21st anniversary of Pop The Cap — the law that lifted North Carolina's 6% ABV ceiling and made the modern NC beer scene possible — then walk to the ballpark for a 6:45 first pitch.

morning.title: Walk on the Wild Side
morning.location: Sarah P. Duke Gardens, 420 Anderson St, Durham
morning.notes: An hour in the Blomquist Garden of Native Plants with horticulture staff. Book ahead — these walks cap at a small group.

morning.title: Mystery Beer Thursdays
morning.location: The Glass Jug Beer Lab (RTP), 5410 NC-55, Durham
morning.notes: Runs all day from 11 AM. A $5 blind pour — the cheapest interesting thing on this itinerary, 20 minutes south in RTP if you're coming from that direction.

afternoon.title: Historic Stagville Guided Tour
afternoon.location: Historic Stagville State Historic Site, 5828 Old Oxford Hwy, Durham
afternoon.notes: Twenty minutes north of downtown. One of the largest plantations in the antebellum South, told through the lives of the people enslaved there. Weekday tours at 11 and 1.

evening.title: Pop The Cap Turns 21!
evening.notes: 5–7:30 PM, which lines up exactly with a 6:45 first pitch if you leave at 6:15. Twenty-one years since North Carolina lifted its 6% ABV cap — the reason every strong beer in this state exists.

evening.title: Durham Bulls vs Memphis Redbirds
evening.location: Durham Bulls Athletic Park, 409 Blackwell St, Durham
evening.notes: Game three of the Memphis series. The DBAP is a 10-minute walk from Fullsteam — leave the car where it is.

evening.title: Pony Run Thursdays with Fleet Feet
evening.location: Ponysaurus Brewing Co., 219 Hood St, Durham
evening.notes: Alternative evening if baseball isn't the draw: a free group run from Ponysaurus with beer at the finish, open to all paces.

food.vegan_dish: Vegetable ramen ordered with a vegetable broth — confirm with the kitchen, as the default broths are pork-based
food.vegetarian_dish: Vegetable ramen or the small plates upstairs in the izakaya
food.notes: 415 E Chapel Hill St, central to everything on this route. The upstairs izakaya has the more flexible menu.

food.vegan_dish: Ballpark vegan options are thin — eat before you go, or ask at the Bull City Burger stand, which has run a plant-based patty in past seasons
food.vegetarian_dish: Standard ballpark fare plus a few local vendor stands
food.notes: Honest answer: the ballpark is not where the good vegan food is. Fullsteam is a 10-minute walk and has food trucks most evenings — check which truck is parked before you commit.

food.vegan_dish: Truck-dependent — Durham's rotation includes several fully plant-based trucks, so it's worth checking Fullsteam's schedule the day of
food.vegetarian_dish: Truck-dependent
food.notes: Eat here before the game rather than at the park. The truck lineup is posted on the brewery's own calendar.

alternatives.leg: Durham Bulls game (6:45 PM, outdoor ballpark)
alternatives.good_weather: Open-air Triple-A baseball with the Lucky Strike tower behind left field.
alternatives.rain: Bulls games are delayed rather than cancelled where possible; if it's called, Fullsteam's Pop The Cap event runs to 7:30 indoors, and the Carolina Theatre and Motorco are both a short walk away.
The Nasher Museum is five minutes away on Duke's campus and is indoors.

practical_notes: This is the one day in the window with no National Weather Service forecast — the NWS 7-day gridpoint forecast for Raleigh ends August 12. Check the forecast the morning of; every outdoor leg here has an indoor alternative.
Book the Duke Gardens walk ahead; it's $10 and capacity-limited.
Duke Gardens parking is paid and fills on weekday mornings — the Anderson Street lot is closest to the Blomquist Garden.
Park once downtown: Fullsteam, the ballpark and the American Tobacco Campus are all walkable from the same decks.
Historic Stagville is closed Sunday and Monday; Thursday tours run at 11 AM and 1 PM only.
